Rule: on a touch screen, in a story with slides (the Lab, the tour), the gesture chooses the step. A swipe released under 2.5 px/ms is exactly one step (shown once the page has gone 32 px under the finger; its momentum is held on that step's rest, unseen because the stage is sticky); a flick (2.5 px/ms and up) stays free, steps shown 120 ms late, never settling behind the step it showed; a swipe that brings a story on lands on the step at its door; leaving by the end steps is native scroll. No touch is taken, no lock. The statement stays position-driven. Where a put page is not known to stay put under a fling (non-Chromium: Safari, Firefox) nothing is put until the scroll rests. Steps cost 0.85 of the mouse's hold (was 0.6).
